points.description: Valid conclusion from the data: plastic B stretched the most (about 22–23 mm) and plastic A the least (10–12 mm); ranking B > D > C > A (most to least stretchable). Must be supported by data. Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only the most or least stretchable plastic is identified, or the conclusion is correct but not supported with data.

levels.says: Identifies only the most or least stretchable plastic, or gives a correct conclusion without data support.

points.description: First valid improvement to design/validity, e.g. more trials (more than two) and averaging; use identical sample size/dimensions/thickness for all plastics; use the same fixed weight stated and controlled; measure more precisely or time accurately.

Second, different valid improvement from the same kind of list (e.g. control temperature, test more samples of each plastic, specify and keep the same mass of weights, use the same length/width of samples). Must be distinct from P2.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a data-supported conclusion (B most stretchy, A least) plus two distinct, valid improvements. Part marks for incomplete conclusions. Repeating the same improvement in different words earns only one mark.
rubric.answer_key: Conclusion: Plastic B stretched the most (22 and 23 mm) and plastic A the least (10 and 12 mm); order of stretchability B > D > C > A. Improvements: (1) do more trials and average the results; (2) control variables, e.g. use samples of identical size/thickness and state the same weight mass for every plastic (also constant temperature).
